sourceEvidence.claim: The inflammation definition — eliminate the initial cause, remove necrotic cells, initiate tissue repair; divided into acute and chronic; the harmful triple (excessive septic shock, prolonged TB, inappropriate SLE)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Response to eliminate initial cause of cell injury, to remove necrotic cells resulting from the
original insult, and to initiate tissue repair. Divided into acute and chronic. The inflammatory
response itself can be harmful to the host if the reaction is excessive (eg, septic shock), prolonged
(eg, persistent infections such as TB), or inappropriate (eg, autoimmune diseases such as SLE).

Rubor and calor

sourceEvidence.claim: Tumor — swelling; endothelial contraction/disruption → ↑ vascular permeability → protein-rich exudate from postcapillary venules → ↑ interstitial oncotic pressure; leukotrienes (C4, D4, E4), histamine, serotonin, bradykinin
sourceEvidence.quote:
Tumor

Swelling. Endothelial contraction/disruption (eg, from tissue damage) → ↑ vascular permeability
→ leakage of protein-rich fluid from postcapillary venules into interstitial space (exudate)
→ ↑ interstitial oncotic pressure. Endothelial cell contraction is mediated by leukotrienes (C4, D4,
E4), histamine, serotonin, bradykinin.

sourceEvidence.claim: The ESR mechanism — RBCs separated via ⊝ charges; fibrinogen coats RBCs → ↓ ⊝ charge → ↑ aggregation; denser aggregates fall faster → ↑ ESR; co-tested with CRP (more specific)
sourceEvidence.quote:
RBCs normally remain separated via ⊝ charges. Products of inﬂammation (eg, fibrinogen) coat
RBCs → ↓ ⊝ charge → ↑ RBC aggregation. Denser RBC aggregates fall at a faster rate within a
pipette tube → ↑ ESR. Often co-tested with CRP (more specific marker of inflammation).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The acute inflammation definition — transient and early, neutrophils in tissue A with edema, rapid onset (seconds to minutes), short duration (minutes to days), innate immune system (less specific than chronic)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Transient and early response to injury or infection. Characterized by neutrophils in tissue A ,
often with associated edema. Rapid onset (seconds to minutes) and short duration (minutes to
days). Represents a reaction of the innate immune system (ie, less specific response than chronic
inflammation).
